title: Before you start
note: About 2 minutes, before the video. Two background questions (b1 screens out people who took a reinforcement learning course: they are flagged, not stopped) and three knowledge items. The items measure prior knowledge on neighbouring ideas (an average payoff, regret, and how sample size changes a confidence interval, the idea behind UCB's bonus), not the practice or test items, so they don't prime them. Each has an 'I don't know' option to cut guessing. Answers stay on the server; nothing is shown back.

items.prompt: Have you taken a course on reinforcement learning?
Before today, had you heard of multi-armed bandits?
options: Yes, I know roughly how they work

items.prompt: A game pays 10 francs with probability 0.2 and nothing otherwise. If you play it many times, what do you win per game on average?
In a multi-armed bandit problem, what is the "regret" of a strategy?
options: How often it changes its mind about the best option
The reward it missed compared with always choosing the best option
The reward it collects from options that turn out to be bad
How long it takes to find the best option

items.prompt: You estimate the true average of a noisy sensor twice: once from 10 readings and once from 1,000 readings. How do the two 95% confidence intervals for the true average compare?
options: The one from 10 readings is wider
The one from 1,000 readings is wider
It depends only on the average itself
